title: Certificates of Deposit: when an unfunded certificate is closed
content:
## Scope

This clause of the Certificates of Deposit opening policy governs a certificate that was opened but whose opening deposit has not posted. It applies to every tier, each tier supplying its own funding window in calendar days.

## Policy clause

A certificate still in applied status is closed as unfunded once the tier's funding window, in calendar days, has passed after the certificate was opened.

## How the days are counted

- **Starting event:** the opening of the certificate, as shown by the certificate's opening date in the bank's records.
- **Counting:** calendar days are counted with the day after the opening date as day 1.
- **When the lapse is due:** on the date that is the opening date plus the funding window in calendar days, and on any later date. The comparison is "on or after", so the boundary day itself makes the lapse due.
- **What is lapsed:** only a certificate still in applied status. Once the opening deposit has posted, the certificate is active and this clause does not apply to it.
- **Outcome:** the certificate moves from applied to closed, as unfunded.

## Boundary cases (illustrative window of 4 calendar days, not a tier value)

Opening date 1 March; day 1 is 2 March, and the opening date plus 4 days is 5 March.

| Current date | Day count after opening | Certificate still applied? | Lapse due? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 March | day 3 | Yes | No, the boundary day has not been reached |
| 5 March | day 4 | Yes | Yes, the boundary day itself |
| 7 March | day 6 | Yes | Yes |
| 7 March | day 6 | No, the opening deposit posted on 3 March | Not applicable, the certificate is active |

## Points of judgement

**Are business days or calendar days counted?**
Calendar days. Weekends and other non-business days count toward the window.

**Is the window counted from the day the customer asked about the certificate, or from the funding request?**
Neither. It is counted from the certificate's opening date as recorded by the bank.
